_meta.indication: KRYSTEXXA (pegloticase) is a PEGylated uric acid specific enzyme indicated for the treatment of chronic gout in adult patients refractory to conventional therapy.
_meta.receipt_date: October 31, 2008 (original BLA submission); resubmission received March 15, 2010

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled efficacy and safety study; subjects assigned 2:2:1 to 8 mg pegloticase every 2 weeks, 8 mg pegloticase every 4 weeks, and placebo every 2 weeks over the 24-week treatment period.
pivotal_trials.population: Hyperuricemic (serum uric acid >= 8 mg/dL) adults (>= 18 years) with symptomatic gout refractory to conventional therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percentage of subjects achieving and maintaining PUA concentrations less than 6 mg/dL for at least 80% of the time during months 3 and 6 combined.
pivotal_trials.n: Study 405: 8 mg/2 wks N=43; placebo N=20
pivotal_trials.result: Responders on 8 mg/2 wks: 20 (47%) vs 0 (0%) placebo; 95% CI for difference (32%, 61%); p<0.001.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled efficacy and safety study; subjects assigned 2:2:1 to 8 mg pegloticase every 2 weeks, 8 mg pegloticase every 4 weeks, and placebo every 2 weeks over the 24-week treatment period.
pivotal_trials.population: Hyperuricemic (serum uric acid >= 8 mg/dL) adults (>= 18 years) with symptomatic gout refractory to conventional therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percentage of subjects achieving and maintaining PUA concentrations less than 6 mg/dL for at least 80% of the time during months 3 and 6 combined.
pivotal_trials.n: Study 406: 8 mg/2 wks N=42; placebo N=23
pivotal_trials.result: Responders on 8 mg/2 wks: 16 (38%) vs 0 (0%) placebo; 95% CI for difference (23%, 53%); p<0.001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=5%): gout flares, infusion reactions, nausea, contusion or ecchymosis, nasopharyngitis, constipation, chest pain, anaphylaxis and vomiting. Anaphylaxis occurred in 6.5% of patients on 8 mg every 2 weeks (vs none placebo); infusion reactions in 26% (vs 5% placebo).
target_moa: Pegloticase is a PEGylated recombinant uricase (urate oxidase) enzyme that reduces serum urate by metabolizing uric acid to allantoin and hydrogen peroxide; humans lack endogenous uricase.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: ANAPHYLAXIS AND INFUSION REACTIONS - anaphylaxis and infusion reactions have been reported during and after administration; administer in healthcare settings by providers prepared to manage anaphylaxis; pre-medicate with antihistamines and corticosteroids.

rems.type: REMS approved, consisting of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and a timetable for submission of assessments.

advisory_committee.vote: Combined advisory committee held June 16, 2009 voted 14 to 1 in favor of approval.

description.text: Added co-administration of methotrexate (15 mg oral once weekly) in treatment of chronic gout in adult patients refractory to conventional therapy

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for revisions to the Prescribing Information and Medication Guide adding co-administration of methotrexate (15 mg oral once weekly, for patients for whom methotrexate is not contraindicated and clinically appropriate) in treatment of chronic gout in adult patients refractory to conventional therapy.

summary.text: Pegloticase received orphan drug designation (2001) for chronic refractory gout and was granted priority review. Approval followed a prior complete response letter (July 31, 2009) for product quality/manufacturing deficiencies, resolved on resubmission; a combined advisory committee voted 14 to 1 in favor of approval.

citations.quote: This is an orphan indication and an orphan designation was granted in 2001.
The application was subsequently granted priority review and an advisory committee meeting was scheduled.
A complete response action was taken on July 31, 2009, primarily due to deficiencies related to product quality and manufacturing.
The panel voted 14 to 1 in favor of approval.

requirement.text: An observational safety study enrolling 500 patients treated with Krystexxa for one year duration, in patients with hyperuricemia and gout refractory to standard uric acid-lowering therapies.

requirement.text: Redevelop the anti-PEG antibody ELISA assay to address high intra- and inter-assay variability.

citations.quote: 6. The current anti-PEG antibody ELISA shows a very high degree of intra- and inter-assay variability possibly related to the PEG coating of the ELISA plate. This indicates either that the assay is not sufficiently optimized or that the format is unsuitable. Redevelop the anti-PEG antibody assay to address these concerns.
